subject: Long-horizon anchor approval for Skyline Health — DL-4729
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Long-horizon anchor approval for Skyline Health — DL-4729

Team,

Quick ask: Skyline (attached SOW + offer) is asking for a 4-year price lock on their core inference plan at current list rates with a 3% annual uplift cap and an explicit "renewal protection" clause (no more than a 5% step change at renewal, and the ability to reprice only if material changes to SLAs or usage patterns). They are proposing a $3.5M committed spend over 4 years (paid annually).

Why this is time-sensitive:
- Rival vendor (CloudScale) has submitted a counteroffer that includes a 3yr lock + higher uplift; Skyline has signaled urgency to finalize next-week procurement cycle.
- Skyline is a strategic healthcare account in our west region (potential to expand to Dedicated private infra later).

What deal desk needs from execs:
1) Executive OK to sign a 4-year price lock at current effective unit rates with a hard uplift cap of 3%/year.
2) Approval to include a renewal protection clause limited to specified conditions (SLAs, material usage delta).
3) Confirmation that the 4-year term with the commit level is acceptable from finance; if not, any mandatory minimum commit % or escrow requirement.

Attachments: Skyline_SOW_v3.pdf, Redwood_Offer_Summary_DL4729.xlsx

Recommended from Sales: approve — this preserves expansion runway and wins a named health system where switching costs are non-trivial.

Asks: Marissa — please confirm deal desk view. Kimberly — need your finance visibility/guardrails. Jonas — please confirm capacity/priority implications for Dedicated instances if we later migrate them.

Thanks,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales — West
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Long-horizon anchor approval for Skyline Health — DL-4729

Mateo — thanks for the summary. Deal desk has reviewed the commercials and the risks. Concise notes: 

- This meets our threshold for strategic multi-year anchor requests (>$3M over term), but the uplift cap request is outside the standard 2-year guardrails (we typically allow 2 years with a 4% uplift cap).
- Recommended path: escalate for exec signoff with the following optional mitigations if needed:
  * Require a 25% minimum first-year prepayment or a Letter of Credit for year 1
  * Add a contract clause that allows a mid-term repricing if aggregate qps/token usage exceeds a 2.5x baseline for two consecutive months
- Legal flagged neutral language around "renewal protection"; they recommend a narrowly-scoped clause rather than an open-ended guarantee.

If execs sign off, we will prepare the final SOW and push for DocuSign by EOD Friday to meet Skyline procurement timeline.

Marissa
Sr. Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Long-horizon anchor approval for Skyline Health — DL-4729

Folks — after reviewing finance model and downside scenarios, I can provide conditional executive approval with the following conditions: 

1) Acceptance of a 4-year price lock with a 3% annual uplift cap is permitted provided Skyline signs a minimum committed spend equal to at least 70% of the $3.5M in year 1 (i.e., $2.45M) or provides a Letter of Credit for unbilled committed amounts.
2) Renewal protection will be limited: "Redwood will limit list-rate increases at renewal to no more than 5% unless materially different service requirements are requested by the customer (e.g., dedicated private deployment, materially higher SLOs)." We will include explicit metrics that define "material."
3) Include a mid-term usage review clause allowing Redwood to re-open commercials if usage exceeds the baseline by >250% for two consecutive months (mitigation Marissa suggested).
4) All terms subject to legal redline. I attached Finance_Redline_DL4729.docx with tracked changes on the payment schedule and escrow language.

If Marissa can confirm we can contractually require the min-first-year payment / LOC, I will turn this to "Approved" for the purposes of Deal Desk execution.

Kimberly Park
VP, Finance & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Finance_Redline_DL4729.docx

Mateo / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for incorporating our needs into the SOW. We confirm Skyline is willing to sign a 4-year agreement with the 3% uplift cap and the renewal-protection language as you described, subject to: 

- We will provide a year-1 payment of $2.5M on countersignature (slightly above the 70% threshold Kimberly requested).
- Legal requests a brief window (48 hours) to review the finance redline and minor language changes to define "material" service changes cited in the renewal protection clause.

Next steps on our end: we will circulate internal approval and return countersigned DocuSign by EOD Tuesday. Please send final DocuSign packet with the Finance redline incorporated and a final SOW (PDF).

Appreciate the team's flexibility — Skyline is eager to move forward.

Alicia Park
